governments.label: None / Unclaimed
governments.hint: Unclaimed land: no state at all. The manpower model reads the lowest extraction row.

governments.label: Chiefdom
governments.hint: A paramount chief redistributes what he can see. Low extraction; nearly everyone counts as free.

governments.label: Tribal Confederacy
governments.hint: Allied kin groups under a war leader. Low extraction; nearly everyone counts as free.

governments.label: Monarchy
governments.hint: One ruler and an administrative court over free peasants and a tied substrate.

governments.label: Oligarchy
governments.hint: Rule by a few families; a narrow citizen body. The least-grounded citizen row.

governments.label: Republic
governments.hint: Elected magistrates taxing a small area intensively; half the population are citizens.

governments.label: Theocracy
governments.hint: Rule by a priesthood (the Papal States, the prince-bishoprics). Reads as Monarchy in the manpower model.

governments.label: Empire
governments.hint: A professional revenue service over conquered subjects; the narrowest citizen body.

governments.label: City-State
governments.hint: One city and its hinterland, taxed intensively; a slave-holding citizen body.

governments.label: Merchant Republic
governments.hint: Venice, Genoa, Novgorod. Reads as Republic in the manpower model; the trade framing is not modelled yet.

governments.label: City League
governments.hint: The Hanseatic and Lombard leagues: strong towns, weak centre, no common treasury. Lower extraction than a monarchy.

governments.label: Sacral Monarchy
governments.hint: A ruler whose authority is sacred (Byzantium, the Caliphate). A little more extraction than Monarchy; its religion is not modelled.

governments.label: Holy Order
governments.hint: A military-monastic order (the Teutonic Order). Reads as Oligarchy in the manpower model.

governments.label: Feudal Realm
governments.hint: Revenue and troops sit with the vassals (Capetian France). A weak centre: lower extraction than Monarchy.

governments.label: Nomadic Khanate
governments.hint: The Mongols, the Turkic khaganates. Low extraction, but its levy of free horsemen reaches further (a levy bonus, no larger standing army).

governments.label: Military Regime
governments.hint: The army is the state (the Mamluks, the Tokugawa bakufu). High extraction; Empire's citizen body.

governments.label: Tributary Hegemony
governments.hint: Tribute from nominally autonomous subjects (the Aztec Triple Alliance). Extraction without administration; Empire's citizen body.
